questions.q: Where was Ezekiel when the hand of the Lord Yahweh fell on him?
questions.a: Ezekiel was sitting in his house, with the elders of Judah sitting before him.

questions.q: Where did the Spirit take Ezekiel, and what did he see there?
questions.a: The Spirit took Ezekiel to the inner Northern Gate in Jerusalem, where he saw the idol that provokes jealousy.

questions.q: What did the Spirit say he was being forced to do because of the great abominations (wickedness) of the house of Israel?
questions.a: The Spirit said he was being forced to go far from his own sanctuary.

questions.q: After Ezekiel dug into the wall and saw a door, what did the Spirit tell Ezekiel to do?
questions.a: The Spirit to Ezekiel to, “Go and see the wicked abominations that they are doing here.”

questions.q: What were the elders saying about Yahweh as they worshiped their idols?
questions.a: The elders were saying that Yahweh does not see them and that Yahweh had forsaken the land.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel see the women doing at the gate on the north side of Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: The women were sitting there mourning for Tammuz.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel see in the inner courtyard of Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: There were twenty-five men with their faces to the east worshiping Shamesh.

questions.q: Because of the abominations of the house of Israel, what did the Spirit say he was going to do?
questions.a: The Spirit said that he would act and not spare them, nor have compassion even though they cry with a loud voice.

commentary.text: The idolatries committed by the Jewish rulers. (Ezek. 8:1-6) The superstitions to which the Jews were then devoted, the Egyptian. (Ezek. 8:7-12) The Phoenician. (Ezek. 8:13,14) The Persian. (Ezek. 8:15,16) The heinousness of their sin. (Ezek. 8:17,18)

Ezek. 8:1-6 The glorious personage Ezekiel beheld in vision, seemed to take hold upon him, and he was conveyed in spirit to Jerusalem. There, in the inner court of the temple, was prepared a place for some base idol. The whole was presented in vision to the prophet. If it should please God to give any man a clear view of his glory and majesty, and of all the abominations committing in any one city, he would then admit the justice of the severest punishments God should inflict thereon.

Ezek. 8:7-12 A secret place was, as it were, opened, where the prophet saw creatures painted on the walls, and a number of the elders of Israel worshipped before them. No superiority in worldly matters will preserve men from lust, or idolatries, when they are left to their own deceitful hearts; and those who are soon wearied in the service of God, often grudge no toil nor expense when following their superstitions. When hypocrites screen themselves behind the wall of an outward profession, there is some hole or other left in the wall, something that betrays them to those who look diligently. There is a great deal of secret wickedness in the world. They think themselves out of God's sight. But those are ripe indeed for ruin, who lay the blame of their sins upon the Lord.

Ezek. 8:13-18 The yearly lamenting for Tammuz was attended with infamous practices; and the worshippers of the sun here described, are supposed to have been priests. The Lord appeals to the prophet concerning the heinousness of the crime; "and lo, they put the branch to their nose," denoting some custom used by idolaters in honour of the idols they served. The more we examine human nature and our own hearts, the more abominations we shall discover; and the longer the believer searches himself, the more he will humble himself before God, and the more will he value the fountain open for sin, and seek to wash therein.
